utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, can you indicate to me whether there is a joint Defence position in relation to the motion affecting K73?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There is a joint position. There is a joint position, and it's different than Mr. Hannis's position. We have a dispute over the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should we grant it, so you oppose it, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We oppose it but we have an alternative proposal to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does the discussion of this require to be in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It may in part, if -- for I may have to make submissions in connection with the confidential annex A. To that extent we will have to be in closed session but for the rest of my submissions it can be in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, please carry on and you should tell me when we require to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, at present, K-73 has a pseudonym and image distortion. We oppose the request for closed session but we submit that adding the protection of voice distortion will suffice thereby allowing the witness to have the protection he feels he needs, and allowing the accused to benefit to the right to a public trial. Rule 75(B)(i)(c) and (d) provide giving testimony through image or voice altering devices and the assignment of a pseudonym of the that's the basis for our request. We submit that the overriding interest here is the public nature of these proceedings. The measures we propose protect the identity of K-73 and they address his concerns. However, his testimony, the nature and the content of his testimony, must be public in our submission. We take issue with the factors raised by the Prosecution in their confidential annex A and to address those, Your Honour, we will need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. For the purpose of addressing the confidential material, we will have private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are satisfied that K-73's persistent concern and anxiety about the security of relatives is justified on the basis of the material presented to us, and for that reason, we will grant the application to hear his evidence in closed session. We have, of course, in the past in this case already reviewed orders of a similar nature when it transpired that perhaps we had been overcautious, and obviously if that were to emerge in this case then the evidence would become public, but as presently advised, we consider that the appropriate course to follow is to hear the evidence in closed session. The effect of that of course is that this evidence cannot be reported out with this courtroom in any form that is not absolutely essential for the purpose of conducting these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, we'll now return to the cross-examination of the current witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lami. Can you hear me? No? No translation? Good afternoon, Mr. Lami.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry that you had to wait but we had a matter of law to deal with and that has been dealt with and we can proceed with your evidence. Please remember that the solemn declaration to tell the truth which you gave at the outset of your evidence continues to apply to the evidence today. And Mr. Visnjic will now cross-examine. Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I don't know if we are in public session now. Are we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have been in public session, including the announcement of the decision in relation to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lami. I'm Tomislav Visnjic. I'm defence counsel for Mr. Ojdanic and I'm going to put some questions to you in relation to a photograph. Could the witness please be shown 3D94, page 1 of that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm familiar with those photos, I will describe what you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't know how much you can see, but do you find anything familiar in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness please be shown page 2?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know that because where I'm from, there are no such pines.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lami, do you find this photograph to be familiar?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at photograph number 3, or page 3. Mr. Lami, this should be a hill between Lama and Vata. Is there a hill?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you can tell now on the basis of this. Could that be it? The picture was taken from the direction of Dubrava, though.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know if you can see that. This is where my house is, and this is where the meadows are, and the Pragas were here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that calls for three coloured pencils, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is quite interesting, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you please take another look at the previous photograph once again, please? Looking at the transcript now, it would be page 2 again, then. Mr. Lami, if you have a look at this, do you find it familiar now? What do we see on this photograph now?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house of Rrahman Mema who was massacred here. This is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, please wait for the witness to finish; we could not hear what he was saying, interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the house of Rrahman Lami or Lama. This is the barn of Rrahman Lama that was burnt. When the Serbs left, they torched the barn.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'll put a question to you now. Let me ask you: Can you see in this picture where the KLA positions were, the place where the KLA positions were as described in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: KLA was positioned after this house, where you can see this other house. There is this road that divides the two houses and they stayed there only three days. On the 12th they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What you're saying to me now is that the KLA was behind the hill and that in fact you cannot see their positions from this particular location, am I right?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, my house is here. You can see that. Then you can see the top of the roof of a house of one of my cousins. This is where our army, the KLA, was stationed. The massacre was committed in that hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you mark where the KLA positions were on this photograph? Put a circle there, please.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA didn't have any positions, because they left the village, that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, where were their trenches?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their trenches were dug here; here, that's where they were dug but they had not been completed. They left the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lami, you need to write on the photograph or on the screen rather for the photograph to be marked. Can you actually make a circle or a similar mark where you say these trenches had been begun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see the trenches very well but this is the direction where they were. There was a meadow where they were dug. You see where these houses -- these trees are. They didn't finish. They started digging the trenches but they didn't finish them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've marked a house with a little blue dot on the chimney and you've marked the trenches near the trees with a slightly bigger blue mark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lami, can you just put number 1 next to the place where you think the trenches were? That would do. Because I don't find this to be very clear. Perhaps I don't have the same picture. Could you please put a number 1 next to the point where you think the trenches were?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no trenches actually. When they started to defend themselves, they did that in this place where the trees are. Shall I put a number here?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: There. Place a number 1 there?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number 1, then. This doesn't write very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions in relation to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it please be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC 36, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Lami. Now let us move on to the next page of this exhibit. This was page number 3. And you said that you recognised this to be the hill between Lama and Vata.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Vata is from this side here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I still haven't got anything on my screen. Is this the hill, the photograph at page 3 of this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the hill in our part. This is our hill, the hill of our village. This is where the asphalt is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lami, I will show you a few other photographs. We will take them in order. Could we please see number 4 now? Or, rather, let us move on to number 5, since these two are the same.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: We've already seen this exhibit. Let's drop it. Could we now please show 3D96 to the witness? Page 2.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recognise this place. It's in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I warranted to ask you this: This photograph on page 2, is this supposed to be Vata? Is this the right side of that hill? Let us try with page 3. Perhaps that photograph is a bit better.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses are along the asphalt road. They are part of Vata as well but there are not so many houses here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at page 4 of this exhibit. Mr. Lami, do you recognise these houses?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are called Neziraj houses. They are in upper Vata. And here is the asphalt road that leads to Tetova.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please show 3D95 to the witness and let us begin with page 2. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise the photographs. This is the martyrs' cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What can you recognise in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a monument. Here is Ilir Caka, here is Rrahman Mema, and Hebib. There are four monuments built there, tombstones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: This cemetery, Mr. Lami, it's got nothing to do with the event you mentioned in your statement. Am I correct to conclude that?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the graves of the persons that I'm here to testify about, Rrahman Lami, Hebib Lami, Mahmut Caka. I cannot recognise the tombstones, what is written on them, because it's kind of foggy, the picture is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: We'll try to blow it up a bit, but since you seem to know who the persons buried are, let us move on to page 3 of this exhibit. Page 4, please. This is as good a photograph as we can obtain from blowing it up. In any case, Mr. Lami, you have identified for me the people buried whose four tombstones we see here.

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first photograph was clearer. This is Rrahman here. I cannot recognise this one here. Can you go back to the first photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This isn't an exercise in nostalgia. Do we need to go into this any further, Mr. Visnjic, or have you got the information you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'm about to conclude. I have received sufficient information from the witness. And this would also be my last question for the witness. I tried to use this witness to identify certain locations and their names, since while we were taking photographs we were not sure what we were taking photographs of, and I basically made use of Mr. Lami's presence here to try and clarify that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Lami.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How do you know how it is that Mahmut Caka, Hebib Lami, and Brahim Lami came to be buried in that cemetery?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are very close with them. It's only 1.000 metres between us. We invite each others on weddings, we go to pay condolences in cases of death. We are neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. That cemetery, I think you referred to it as a martyrs' cemetery. What I want to know is do you know how it is they came to be buried in that cemetery, which is a martyrs' cemetery?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were buried there because other graves are there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether or not they were members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not they specifically speaking they bore arms at all for any organisation?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially these four persons, one of them was an invalid from his birth, and the others were helping him. That person was a student, Brahim Lami was his name. They had no weapons whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, that answer, you said there were no weapons whatsoever. Are you referring to the particular day of the incident, that's the 13th of April, 1999, or in general? In general did they bear arms for the KLA or any armed group?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about other dates, but for 13th of April, when the offensive took place, I saw them, and this invalid was walking and the other three persons were helping him and when they entered the forest, that's where the Serb army captured them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I suspect you've answered my question but I just want to be absolutely clear. I was asking you about whether or not you knew of them bearing arms for the KLA or any organisation at any time?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see them carry KLA weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Lami, you referred to the cemetery as a martyrs cemetery. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SEJDI LAMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are civilians who are buried in the martyrs cemetery. They have nothing to do with KLA or any other organisation. They were killed during the war and that's why we call them martyrs. They did not die by natural death but they were killed by the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does anyone wish to ask any questions arising out of that answer? Very well. Thank you, Mr. Lami. That completes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, our next witness will be K-73 and this will be in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall go into closed session for the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
